summary: Byambyn Rinchen was a scholar in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Tibetology. He studied at the Leningrad Orient Institute (~1924–1927) and Eötvös Loránd University (~1955–1956), and held a post at the National University of Mongolia.
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Byung-gon Kim studied at Rissho University (attested 2007). He serves at Minobusan University as a professor, dean, and research institute director (attested 2026).

C. C. Berg worked in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (beginning 1919) under doctoral supervisors G. A. J. Hazeu and Nicolaas Johannes Krom, serving as Professor of Javanese at Leiden (1929–1972).

C. Collin Davies worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned a B.A. from Aberystwyth University (~1919–1922) and a Ph.D. from Peterhouse (~1923–1926), later serving as Lecturer at SOAS (1926–1936) and Reader at Oxford (1936–1963).

A scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology, C. D. Sebastian earned a PhD from Banaras Hindu University, studying under Paul Williams, Gavin D'Costa, and others. He was Professor of Indian Philosophy at IIT Bombay (attested 2016).

C. Kunhan Raja worked in Indology and philosophy. He earned a D.Phil. at Oxford under Arthur Anthony Macdonell, became the first Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Madras (1927), and was Honorary Director of the Adyar Library (attested 1928–1938).
C. M. Naim worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley (~1959–1961) and served as Professor Emeritus at the University of Chicago (~2001–2025).

C. M. Ridding worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Girton College and the University of Cambridge, studying under Edward Byles Cowell and T. W. Rhys Davids, she worked at Girton College (1904) and Cambridge University Library (1911).
C. Peter Bankart is a scholar in Buddhist studies and related fields. He held an affiliation at Wabash College (attested 2003) and served as a Visiting Researcher at Dartmouth College.

C. Pierce Salguero works in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University, and has held posts at the University of Pennsylvania (2011–2012) and Pennsylvania State University (beginning 2010).

C. R. Krishnamacharlu worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Madras Christian College and Pachaiyappa's College, and held a post at the Archaeological Survey of India (~1915–1943).
C. S. Srinivasachariar worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as a professor at Pachaiyappa's College and at Annamalai University (attested 1932–1933).

C. W. Huntington, Jr. specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (~1980–1986) under Luis Oscar Gómez and Madhav M. Deshpande, later serving as Professor at Hartwick College (~1993–2020).
Caixi Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies who pursued a PhD at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the doctoral supervision of Wadinagala Pannaloka (attested 2026).

Calambur Sivaramamurti worked in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Presidency University under S. Kuppuswami Sastri, later holding posts at the Government Museum Chennai (1935–1946), Indian Museum Kolkata (1946), ASI (~1946–1955), and National Museum New Delhi (attested 1952).

Calvert Watkins worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Harvard, EPHE, and DIAS under Joshua Whatmough, later becoming a professor at Harvard (1959–2003) and Distinguished Professor in Residence at UCLA (2003–2013).

Calvin Thomas worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Leipzig, then taught at Michigan (1879–1896) before serving as Professor of Germanic Languages and Literatures at Columbia (1896–1919).

Cameron Bailey is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Indiana University Bloomington, Florida State University under Bryan J. Cuevas, and at Oxford (Wolfson College) under doctoral supervisor Ulrike Roesler.
Cameron David Warner specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Yudru Tsomu and has held academic posts at Dickinson College, Middlebury College, and Aarhus University.

Cameron Foltz specializes in religious studies and Japanology. He earned an MA at Florida State University (attested 2018), where he studied under Bryan J. Cuevas and Jimmy Yu, and became a Postdoctoral Fellow at Columbia University in 2025.
